$comment: Studio's built-in MCP server is the StudioMCP binary shipped inside Roblox Studio (stdio). On Windows, point the command at StudioMCP.exe in your Studio install: roblox-shell mcp add studio -- "C:\path\to\StudioMCP.exe"
title: Roblox Studio
instructions: 'studio <tool>' calls Roblox Studio's built-in MCP tools: run 'help studio' for the list and 'studio <tool> --help' for parameters. studio_id is filled automatically when exactly one Studio is open (otherwise pass --studio_id from 'studio list_roblox_studios'); datamodel_type defaults to Edit (pass --datamodel_type Server or Client during play). Script commands add structured editing on top: query (find by class/name/tag/property, uncapped JSON lines), prop get/set (values convert to the property's type), new, rm, mv, clone, tag, attr, sel (Studio selection), scripts, instances. Edit commands take paths as arguments or one per stdin line (JSON lines with a path field work too), print the paths they changed, and are each one undo step that is reverted if any target fails. Example: query --class BasePart --where Anchored=false | prop set Anchored true. Changes are real edits to the open place: confirm with the user before modifying it.
setup:
Keep Roblox Studio open with a place loaded and its built-in MCP server enabled. Check with: roblox-shell run 'studio list_roblox_studios'
On Windows, set the StudioMCP.exe path (see: roblox-shell config show).
Your own Luau commands go in the commands/ folder in ~/.agent-shell/roblox/.

studio_id.$jq: (.studios | length) as $n | if $n == 1 then .studios[0].id elif $n == 0 then error("no Roblox Studio is connected") else error("\($n) Studios are open: pass --studio_id (see: studio list_roblox_studios)") end
